subject.title: fix(reef): bound JSONL store file reads to prevent OOM on oversized audit/replay stores

question: Should Reef hard-reject existing audit and replay JSONL stores above 32 MiB, or must it provide a safe owner-supported recovery and retention path before that limit ships?
rationale: The patch changes how persisted stores behave after upgrade; code review cannot choose whether to retain, prune, rotate, or repair audit and replay data without maintainer ownership of those durability semantics.

options.title: Add supported recovery before merge
options.body: Keep the streaming bound and add Reef-owned retention/compaction plus a documented Doctor or operator recovery flow for existing oversized stores.

options.title: Accept fail-closed stores
options.body: Ship the hard rejection only if maintainers explicitly accept that operators must manually repair or replace an oversized audit or replay store.

options.title: Pause the limit
options.body: Defer the hard 32 MiB failure until the persisted-store lifecycle contract is designed and validated.

recommendation.title: Add supported recovery before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the streaming bound and add Reef-owned retention/compaction plus a documented Doctor or operator recovery flow for existing oversized stores.
